analysis:
Only the test file provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/EngineV2BridgeTests.swift changed. The changes add a decodeTable to StubTokenizer (lines ~146-155), a stopStringScope parameter to makeBridge (~443, 462), and new tests at lines 847-899 covering scoped stop-string matching (ReasoningStopScope, ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope, EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence). No production code is touched here, so no change to any trust boundary, key handling, attestation, authorization or cache storage.

Relevant existing coverage: bridgeStampsCacheSalt (lines 761-785) asserts that cacheSalt comes only from the coordinator-supplied cacheScope and that consumer prompt_cache_key and user are ignored. This is consistent with the T-041 mitigation, and the test is unchanged. The new stop-scope tests assert matching behaviour only: stops never match inside reasoning spans, and natural-EOS rendering cannot impersonate a stop string. That is a correctness property, not a security control change.

Remaining integration question: the production implementation of the scoped matchedStopSequence and the stopStringScope plumbing is in other files outside this batch (EngineV2Bridge.swift, ReasoningStopScope). If those changed in this PR, reviewers should confirm that scope handling does not affect the cacheSalt or tenant isolation, and that stop-sequence reporting does not leak reasoning content. No finding is supportable from the supplied evidence.
